key_insight: The Empathy Applicability Framework (EAF) lets models predict, from the patient query alone, whether and how empathy should be expressed—shifting empathy modeling from reactive labeling of doctor replies to anticipatory classification of need.
problem_solved: Existing NLP work focuses on labeling empathy in clinicians' responses and cannot reliably decide ahead of response generation when empathy is appropriate; this causes over- or under-expression of empathy in general health queries.
method: Define a theory-driven taxonomy (EAF) that classifies general health queries by the applicability and style of empathetic response.
Annotate a corpus of general health queries according to the EAF and train classifiers to predict empathy applicability from the query text.
Evaluate models with automatic metrics and human judgments; propose integration points for LLM response policies (when to generate empathetic language vs neutral information).
impact: Provides a practical tool for AI/ML teams to calibrate empathetic behavior in patient-facing LLMs, reducing inappropriate empathy and improving trust and safety in clinical conversational systems.
visual_elements: Taxonomy flowchart showing EAF categories (e.g., Empathy-Required, Empathy-Optional, Empathy-Not-Applicable) with brief decision rules.
Pipeline diagram: Query → EAF classifier → Response policy (empathetic vs informational) → LLM output.
Side-by-side examples: raw query with two model outputs (empathetic vs neutral) and a brief annotation explaining the correct choice.
Performance bar chart comparing classifier accuracy, precision/recall on each EAF category and human satisfaction scores.
paper_title: Empathy Applicability Modeling for General Health Queries
paper_authors: Shan Randhawa, Agha Ali Raza, Kentaro Toyama, Julie Hui, Mustafa Naseem
